tasks.short: Coordinate aircraft movement with adjacent control units by radio or telephone.

steps.what: Check actual aircraft state and current coordination conditions in the approved control display
Formulate and check the exact movement coordination message and intended control-unit recipient
Transmit the exact checked coordination message to the adjacent control unit
Receive and validate the actual adjacent-unit response and continuing movement state
Enter and check the actual coordination outcome in the electronic flight strip
Commit the checked coordination strip entry

tasks.design: Retain approved {OTHER} control displays and electronic strip capture with human coordination through {TELEPHONY}. No new automation changes live coordination, response validation or actual strip entry.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coordination needs current shared traffic understanding.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing electronic strips already support the record.
tasks.still_hard: Rapid state changes and ambiguous or conflicting coordination.
tasks.human_edge: Maintain shared traffic understanding and detect unsafe misunderstandings.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in live coordination or control rights.

evidence.claim: smartSTRIPS replaced paper strips in two Schiphol towers in 2019; this supports an existing electronic record, not automatic live coordination.

assumptions: Boundary is one actual coordination-message cycle with its strip update. Approved surveillance and strips supply actual aircraft identity, position, level and movement state; controller checks these in s1 and produces exact content and destination in s2. Missing or conflicting data use the existing manual procedure, not inferred fields.

Native strip entry inspected and already suitable; no new configuration or upkeep. Provisional shares not measured. The5-unit radio/telephone transmission is real speech time fully retained, not a save-click gain. Adjacent unit assumed same organisation; an outside organisation changes authority to act_external, not effort. Any changed message requires a fresh content check and transmission cycle. Strip accuracy check is ordinary entry, no added approval ceremony; commit1 retained.
unknowns: Actual approved unit workflow and strip-entry effort
research_questions: Is any actual duplicate administrative strip entry present beyond the existing native workflow?

tasks.short: Transfer departing flights and accept arriving flights between control units.

steps.what: Check actual departing or arriving aircraft state, coordination status and transfer conditions
Decide whether to transfer or accept actual control under current conditions
Prepare and check the exact transfer or acceptance message and aircraft identity
Transmit the exact checked transfer or acceptance message to the relevant unit
Verify actual acceptance, handover completion and continuing aircraft responsibility from live responses
Enter and check actual transferred or accepted responsibility in the electronic flight strip
Commit the checked actual transfer strip entry

tasks.design: Keep approved {OTHER} transfer displays and electronic strip entry. The controller decides, checks and transmits the actual handover message, then records responsibility only after actual acceptance is verified.
tasks.previous_blocker: A sent handover request is not accepted control.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing electronic transfer status supports human checks.
tasks.still_hard: Maintaining continuous responsibility during a changing traffic situation.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in transfer or acceptance authority.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: approved electronic flight-strip workflows support control-responsibility records; actual acceptance still requires verified live coordination.

assumptions: Boundary is one departing-transfer or arriving-acceptance cycle through its actual strip update. Existing approved system supplies aircraft identity, actual state and transfer conditions; controller verifies in s1 and captures actual accepted responsibility in s6. A missing response does not become acceptance; use current manual fallback.

tasks.short: Provide pilots with meteorological, navigational and other information by radio.

steps.what: Read actual meteorological, navigational and flight-context information in the approved control display
inputs: actual approved weather and navigation feeds

steps.what: Select and check the exact information, units and aircraft recipient for radio delivery
Transmit the exact checked meteorological or navigational information to the pilot by radio
Receive and check actual pilot acknowledgement or readback against the transmitted information
Enter and check the actual required flight-strip annotation for the information exchange
Commit the checked actual pilot exchange annotation

tasks.design: Retain the approved {OTHER} weather, navigation, radio and strip tools. The controller checks actual information and recipient, transmits, verifies acknowledgement and makes the existing required annotation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Information must be current, relevant and correctly understood.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing approved feeds already provide the source data.
tasks.still_hard: Frequency congestion, changing conditions and misunderstood units.
tasks.human_edge: Detect and correct unsafe misunderstandings in context.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in live pilot communication.
